candidates.exact_span: It is proposed that the permit be reissued for a 5-year term following regulations promulgated at 40 CFR §122.46(a). The previous permit will be expired on October 31, 2021. The permittee submitted their application to EPA on April 13, 2021. The existing permit is administratively continued until this permit is issued.
candidates.computation_change_reason: For Federal FY2025, whether enforceable limits, monitoring obligations, and missing-evidence expectations are drawn from the administratively continued prior permit versus the proposed reissued permit depends on interpreting which permit is operative during the evaluation period.

candidates.exact_span: Regulations contained in 40 CFR §122.44 NPDES permit limits are developed that meet the more stringent of either technology-based effluent limitation guidelines, numerical and/or narrative water quality standard-based effluent limits, or the previous permit.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The applicable enforceable limit for a parameter may come from technology-based guidelines, water quality-based limits (including narrative limits), or the previous permit; different readings of which source controls or how 'more stringent' is applied would change the limit used for compliance comparison and any monitoring tied to those limits.

candidates.exact_span: Technology-based effluent limitations are established in the proposed draft permit for TSS and BOD. Water quality-based effluent limitations are established in the proposed draft permit for E. coli bacteria, pH and TRC.
candidates.computation_change_reason: This passage assigns parameters to technology-based versus water quality-based limit regimes; interpreting it determines which numeric limits are enforceable for each parameter and which monitoring/compliance frameworks apply to TSS, BOD, E. coli, pH, and TRC.

candidates.exact_span: Regulations promulgated at 40 CFR §122.44 (a) require TBELs to be placed in NPDES permits based on ELGs where applicable, on BPJ in the absence of guidelines, or on a combination of the two. In the absence of promulgated guidelines for the discharge, permit conditions may be established using BPJ procedures.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether applicable technology-based limits for this discharge derive from ELGs, BPJ, or a combination affects which numeric TBEL values are enforceable and whether limits are guideline-derived or case-specific best professional judgment.

candidates.exact_span: EPA establishes limitations based on the following technology-based controls: BPT, BCT, and BAT.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Which of BPT, BCT, or BAT applies to a given pollutant or discharge category determines the technology basis and thus the enforceable numeric TBEL that would be compared to reported measurements.
